newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Highlands plans A$190 mln offer.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Highlands plans A$190 mln offer.

text.p: Papua New Guinea gold miner Highlands Gold Ltd said on Friday it had proposed a new restructuring plan, where it would float off a separate company, Highlands Pacific Ltd, that would raise A$190 million through an issue of 190 million shares at A$1 each.
Highlands Pacific would then offer A$107 million for Highland's non-Porgera assets and would take on A$23 million of debt along with the non-Porgera assets.
Highlands said the restructure would leave Highlands Pacific with about A$48 million working capital to fund the development of the Ramu and Frieda projects and the exploration programme.
The company said the capital raising was to be fully underwritten by Merrill Lynch (Australia) Pty Ltd and Wilson HTM Corporate Services Ltd.

"A consortium of PNG institutions which have strongly supported the restructuring will invest up to A$110 million and are expected to have an interest of not less than 50.1 percent at the conclusion of the equity raising," Highlands said in a statement.

Earlier this month, Canada's Placer Dome Inc, which is offering 75 cents a share for Highlands, agreed to the restructuring plan which would leave it with Highlands' 25 percent stake in the Porgera gold mine.

Shareholders of Highlands who accept the takeover offer will be entitled to subscribe for about 60 percent of the issue on the basis of three Highlands Pacific shares for each 10 Highlands shares. Highlands said the issue was subject to the registration of a prospectus in Australia and PNG which is expected to occur in early April 1997.
"As part of the restructure process Highlands Pacific will establish a board that reflects the development and exploration nature of its activities," Highlands said.

The company said the restructure was also subject to a number of conditions including the restructuring not requiring approval of Highlands shareholders, the negotiation of detailed documentation to give effect to the restructuring and completion of underwriting arrangements.
Highlands shares closed three cents firmer at 81 cents.
